title: 第8章 库房账本不对劲
lines: 像是有人拿着钝刀，一寸一寸在骨头里搅。
冷汗瞬间从额头滑落，喉咙里一阵腥甜，她几乎是本能地侧身，避开了那种要命的窒息感。
眼前不是医院白光，也不是实验室的无菌环境。
而是一间破旧潮湿的屋子。
霉味、灰尘、冷风，从四面八方灌进来。
窗纸破了一个大洞，风一吹，发出“哗啦哗啦”的响声。
无数不属于她的记忆，像刀一样刺入神经——
“连下人都可以踩一脚的存在。”
最后一幕，是一碗黑色的药，被强行灌入喉中。
手腕细白，却有一道极细的黑色针孔。
这毒不致命，但会一点点封死经脉，让人“自然废掉”，再被世界遗弃。
一个穿着华丽衣裙的少女站在门口，身后跟着两名丫鬟。
脸上是毫不掩饰的厌恶。
content_zh:
相府的夜，比白天更静。

    静得像一张铺开的网。

    而网，正在收紧。

    继母院中，灯火未熄。

    她端坐在主位，指尖轻轻敲着茶盏。

    “苏晚最近，很不一样。”

    她声音很轻。

    像在说一件无关紧要的事。

    可屋内所有人都知道——

    这不是评价。

    这是“警告”。

    站在下首的管事低声道：

    “夫人，她已经连着几次破局。”

    “老太君一事、宴席一事、还有今日小姐那边……”

    他没说完。

    因为说不下去了。

    每一件事，都不像“巧合”。

    更像——被看穿。

    继母抬眼。

    “那就再给她一个局。”

    她笑了一下。

    “让她，没法再站起来的局。”

    第二日。

    相府传出消息。

    “西院丫鬟春杏，夜里暴毙。”

    尸体被抬出来时，全府震动。

    更震动的，是她手里紧紧攥着的一封信。

    信上写着：

    “毒药已换好，待老太君再服一剂，三日必亡。”

    落款——

    苏晚。

    消息一出，全府哗然。

    “果然是她！”

    “之前救人都是装的！”

    “现在终于露出马脚了！”

    舆论瞬间翻转。

    比之前任何一次都快。

    因为这一次——

    是“证据”。

    继母坐在堂中，缓缓喝茶。

    苏柔站在一旁，眼底藏着兴奋。

    她终于等到了。

    等到苏晚真正“掉下来”的那一刻。

    正厅。

    苏晚被“请”来。

    相爷脸色极沉。

    老太君坐在一旁，脸色仍未完全恢复，却已能说话。

    她看着苏晚，眼神复杂。

    “这信，是你的？”

    太医站在一旁，冷汗直冒。

    继母不急不缓开口：

    “春杏是你院中丫鬟。”

    “信也是从她手中搜出。”

    “苏晚。”

    她看向她。

    “你还有什么可说？”

    空气死寂。

    所有人都等着她崩。

    等她慌。

    等她解释。

    甚至等她跪下。

    苏晚站在中央。

    很安静。

    安静得像这场局与她无关。

    她看了一眼那封信。

    没有碰。

    只是淡淡开口：

    “假的。”

    两个字。

    轻得像风。

    却让继母轻轻一笑。

    “你说是假的？”

    她抬手。

    “那你解释。”

    “春杏为何死？”

    “信为何在她手中？”
content_en:
The night in Xiangfu is quieter than during the day.

    As quiet as a spread out net.

    And the net is tightening.

    In the stepmother's courtyard, the lights were still on.

    She sat at the main seat, tapping the teacup lightly with her fingertips.

    "Su Wan is very different lately."

    Her voice was soft.

    It's like saying something insignificant.

    But everyone in the room knew——

    This is not an evaluation.

    This is a "warning".

    The steward standing at the bottom whispered:

    "Madam, she has broken the game several times in a row."

    "The old lady's matter, the banquet, and today's lady..."

    He didn't finish.

    Because I can't talk anymore.

    Nothing seems like a "coincidence".

    More like – being seen through.

    Stepmother raised her eyes.

    "Then give her another round."

    She smiled.

    "It's a game where she can't stand up again."

    The second day.

    News came from the Prime Minister's Mansion.

    "Chun Xing, the maid of the West Courtyard, died suddenly at night."

    When the body was taken out, the whole government was shocked.

    What was even more shocking was the letter she was holding tightly in her hand.

    The letter reads:

    "The poison has been changed. If the old lady takes another dose, she will die in three days."

    Signing——

    Su Wan.

    As soon as the news came out, the whole government was in an uproar.

    "It's indeed her!"

    “I’ve always pretended to save people before!”

    "Now the trick is finally revealed!"

    Public opinion flipped instantly.

    Faster than ever before.

    Because this time——

    It's "evidence".

    The stepmother was sitting in the hall, drinking tea slowly.

    Su Rou stood aside, excitement hidden in her eyes.

    She finally waited.

    Wait until the moment Su Wan really "falls off".

    main hall.

    Su Wan was "invited".

    The Prime Minister's face was extremely dark.

    The old lady sat aside, her face had not fully recovered, but she was able to speak.

    She looked at Su Wan with complicated eyes.

    "Is this letter yours?"

    The imperial doctor stood aside, sweating profusely.

    The stepmother spoke calmly:

    "Chun Xing is the maid in your courtyard."

    "The letter was also found in her hand."

    "Su Wan."

    She looked at her.

    "What else can you say?"

    The air was dead.

    Everyone was waiting for her to collapse.

    Wait for her to panic.

    Wait for her to explain.

    Even waiting for her to kneel down.

    Su Wan stood in the center.

    Very quiet.

    It was as quiet as if this situation had nothing to do with her.

    She glanced at the letter.

    Not touched.

    Just said lightly:

    "Fake."

    Two words.

    As light as the wind.

    But it made her stepmother smile softly.

    "You said it was fake?"

    She raised her hand.

    "Then explain."

    "Why did Chun Xing die?"

    "Why is the letter in her hand?"
title_en: Chapter 8 Something is wrong with the warehouse account book
